title: Run API routes: submit, stop, status, queue
description: The authenticated worker surface behind UC1b, owning src/index.ts routing. POST /api/runs takes project, epic, base_sha, requested_by, notify and an optional queue flag: it validates the token, resolves the project, asks RunRoom for the lease, and either starts a Run Workflow or refuses with the holder run_id (D22). With queue set, a refused submission parks in the DO and ignites on release, visible to status and expiring on a configurable window. POST /api/runs/:id/stop is a clean stop (D15 semantics: finish the in-flight tick, then review and closeout) and must be enforced at the control plane, never as a message the orchestrator has to read. GET /api/runs and /api/runs/:id report Workflow step state plus lease and gate state. Every refusal is written to dispatch_log with its reason code.
notes:
2026-08-19 18:26 - Scope addition (human decision, 2026-08-19): ONE factory serves MANY projects. Two consequences this tick owns:

1. PROJECT ENROLLMENT IS REQUIRED. Today nothing restricts which repo a run may be submitted for — the bearer token is the only gate, so any token holder could submit any owner/repo and the factory would clone and run it. Add an enrolled-projects table (D1) and reject a submission for an unenrolled project with an actionable error naming the enrolment command. Enrolment records owner/repo plus the credential grade it may use. This is a security boundary, not bookkeeping: it is what stops a leaked token from turning the factory into an arbitrary-code runner for any repo on GitHub.
2. PROJECT IS A FIRST-CLASS KEY EVERYWHERE. The lease is per project (RunRoom idFromName(project+epic)), so two repos run concurrently without contending; runs/signals/dispatch_log all carry project; R2 keys carry it. Do not let any route assume a single implicit project.

Explicitly NOT in scope: parameterising the worker/D1/R2 resource names. One factory per Cloudflare account is the intended constraint (see the design doc), so the fixed names ticks-factory / ticks-factory-artifacts are correct — they just need to be a stated constraint rather than an accident.

acceptance_criteria: A submission on a free project starts a run; on a leased project it refuses naming the holder, and with queue set it parks and later ignites; stop transitions a running run to a clean stop without the orchestrator cooperating; status reports lease, phase and queued submissions; every refusal appears in dispatch_log; all routes reject an absent or wrong bearer token.
closed_reason: Completed: run API routes (submit with queue, clean stop, status list and detail) behind the factory bearer token, with project enrolment as a hard boundary — an unenrolled project is refused rather than cloned — the lease holder surfaced verbatim from afj on refusal, and every refusal written to dispatch_log with a reason code from the closed vocabulary.
